en.name: Plateau pressure (Pplat)
en.shortDescription: Plateau pressure (Pplat) — airway pressure during an end-inspiratory hold, in cmH2O.
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Plateau pressure (Pplat) is the airway pressure measured during an end-inspiratory hold (no gas flow), reflecting the pressure distending the alveoli — the elastic recoil of the lungs and chest wall. It is a key target in lung-protective ventilation (kept ≤ ~30 cmH2O). In source data it is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, obtained by the ventilator during an inspiratory pause. It is recorded in intensive care and anaesthesia for ventilated patients. It is reported in centimetres of water (cmH2O); some ventilators display mbar (1 cmH2O ≈ 0.98 mbar).

## Included Concepts

The set resolves to four concepts: one SNOMED observable entity and three LOINC "Clinical Observation" codes.

- *44782825 / 698822002 — Airway plateau pressure (SNOMED)*: the plateau pressure measured during an inspiratory hold. Vocabulary-agnostic and the default when the source carries no LOINC code.
- *36304439 / 60829-9 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway (LOINC)*: the generic LOINC plateau pressure, context unspecified.
- *36303946 / 76259-1 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway --on ventilator (LOINC)*: the same measurement, with the "on ventilator" context made explicit.
- *21490565 / 60802-6 — Dynamic plateau pressure (LOINC)*: a plateau pressure estimated under dynamic (non-hold) conditions.

The two `Pressure.plateau` LOINC codes are pulled in through their shared LOINC Hierarchy anchor, which covers exactly these two and nothing else.

**Note on units**: reported in **cmH2O** (`44777590 / cm[H2O] — centimeter watercolumn`, UCUM), the recommended unit, with a registered cmH2O↔mbar conversion (1 cmH2O = 0.98 mbar).

## Mapping Notes

- **Default concept** when the source records a plateau pressure (Pplat) without a LOINC code: *44782825 / 698822002 — Airway plateau pressure*.
- **Source carries a LOINC code**: keep it. Use *36303946 / 76259-1 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway --on ventilator* when the source states the patient was on the ventilator, otherwise *36304439 / 60829-9 — Pressure.plateau Respiratory system airway*. In practice these two and the SNOMED concept denote the same measurement — an end-inspiratory hold pressure — so downstream analyses should treat them as one variable.
- **Use *21490565 / 60802-6 — Dynamic plateau pressure* only** when the source explicitly reports a dynamic (non-hold) estimate. Its LOINC component is `Pressure.plateau dynamic`, distinct from the `Pressure.plateau` component of the two codes above.
- Convert mbar to cmH2O (×1.02) before mapping.
- **Not peak, mean or PEEP**: these are distinct pressures in their own concept sets.
